# Review pack: review-software-quality

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-software-quality.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Software Quality

Assesses source code against a local Software Quality Rubric (thresholds plus confirmation), localized
architecture-style and layering guidance, and per-language style guides, and classifies every finding by an
ISO/IEC 25010:2023 sub-characteristic. Four sub-subjects run in one pass; each checklist item keeps its
`subSubject` (`Software Quality`, `Design Patterns`, `Architecture Patterns`, `Coding Standards`).

#### Inputs

The capped, sampled list of non-test source files assigned by `compliance-inventory` (entry points plus
representative files per layer/folder), plus any formatter/analyzer configuration and project-reference files it
lists. Review only those files.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/software-quality-rubric.md` — SQR-01…SQR-37. Always load.
- `references/standards/iso-25010.md` — ISO-01…ISO-40 (classification only). Always load.
- `references/standards/azure-architecture.md` — AAS-01…AAS-20. Always load.
- `references/standards/fowler-bliki.md` — MFB-01…MFB-06. Always load.
- `references/standards/fowler-refactoring-catalog.md` — FRC-01…FRC-23 (remedies only). Always load.
- `references/standards/microsoft-csharp.md` — MSC-01…MSC-24. Load only if C# is detected.
- `references/standards/google-java-style.md` — GJS-01…GJS-34. Load only if Java is detected.
- `references/standards/python-peps.md` — PEP-01…PEP-23. Load only if Python is detected.
- `references/standards/google-typescript-style.md` — GTS-01…GTS-23. Load only if JavaScript/TypeScript is detected.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, the always-loaded standards files, and for each
   detected language its `references/languages/<id>.md` and the standards file it points to. For any other
   language (e.g. JavaScript/TypeScript) use the generic rubric elements only and add
   `localized-standard-gap: no language standard for <language>` to `notes` once.
2. Skip generated and vendored files (`*.g.cs`, `*.Designer.cs`, `*.generated.*`, migrations, `*_pb2.py`, `obj/`,
   `target/`, `build/`, `node_modules/`, `vendor/`, files headed "auto-generated"); note any skipped.
3. Evidence rule: a rubric threshold is a trigger, not a verdict. Fail only when the threshold is exceeded **and**
   reading the code confirms the smell (MFB-05). State the counted value in the evidence excerpt; confidence
   `medium` unless the value is at least twice the threshold.
4. Team conventions: if the target documents its own convention (`.editorconfig`, formatter or Checkstyle config,
   written style guide), judge CS-02/CS-05 consistency against it instead of the guide's default; a documented
   convention the code breaks still fails.
5. Software Quality (SQ-01…SQ-06, SQ-08), Design Patterns (DP-01, DP-02, DP-04…DP-06), Architecture Patterns
   (AP-01…AP-04, AP-06, AP-07) and Coding Standards (CS-01…CS-05): for each check evaluate only the elements it
   lists whose "Applies when" condition holds; if none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason. AP-07 is N/A
   unless at least two independently deployable units are in the files.
6. Retired IDs — SQ-07, AP-05, DP-03, CS-CS-01…05, CS-JV-01…05, CS-PY-01…05 — are not evaluated and not written to
   `checkResults`.
7. Boundaries: don't fail for swallowed, ignored or unchecked errors or resources on security-relevant exception
   paths (review-security-operational SEC-OP-02/SEC-OP-10), blocking on async results or singleton bottlenecks
   (review-performance PERF-02/PERF-08), retries, circuit breakers, timeouts or redundancy (review-reliability),
   repository layout, debt markers or superseded code (review-maintainability), CI gating of analyzers
   (review-software-lifecycle SL-11), API contracts (review-api-design) or externalized configuration
   (review-twelve-factor). Out-of-order workflow execution is judged here (SQR-37 under AP-02; decision D-5,
   2026-11-09); whether the caller is authorized for each step stays with review-security-identity-access SEC-IA-02.
8. Classification: append the best-fitting ISO element to each SQ/DP/AP finding title, e.g.
   `[ISO 25010:2023 Maintainability › Analysability, ISO-29]` (the rubric's ISO column is the default).
9. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md`;
   `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
10. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `SQR-01`); the report script derives `standard` and
    `url` from it, so don't write them. Name the matching FRC remedy (name and ID, e.g. *Extract Function* (FRC-01))
    in `recommendation`; never put an FRC or ISO element in `element`.
11. Note strengths where a module is clearly well factored, a pattern clearly simplifies the design, layering is
    clean, or a file is a good example of its language standard.

#### Output

Labels: don't write `subject` or `subSubject`; the report script takes them from `references/checklist.md`
(the `Subject:` line and the check's `Sub-subject` column). Follow `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/standards/software-quality-rubric.md`

*Load rule: SQR-01…SQR-37. Always load.*

### Compliance Reviewer Software Quality Rubric — local standard

- Level: informational only; severity always comes from the owning check (SKILL.md).
- "Smell" is this rubric's own name for the smell (common industry vocabulary, no source attribution). "—" means
  the element has no smell name.
- **Thresholds are triggers, not verdicts.** Fail only when the threshold is exceeded **and** reading the code
  confirms the smell (MFB-05). Counts are reading estimates: state the counted value in the evidence excerpt and use
  confidence `medium` unless the value is at least twice the threshold. An approved analyzer output (step `02`) may
  support a count but is never required.

#### Thresholds

| Measure | Threshold | Element |
|---|---|---|
| Function length | > 60 logical lines (non-blank, non-comment), or > 30 with ≥ 2 distinct jobs | SQR-01 |
| Estimated cyclomatic complexity | > 15 | SQR-03 |
| Control-flow nesting | > 4 levels | SQR-04 |
| Duplicated block | ≥ 10 consecutive lines in ≥ 2 places | SQR-06 |
| Class or module size | > 500 lines, or > 20 public methods, or > 10 constructor dependencies | SQR-08 |
| Parameters | > 5 (constructor injection excluded) | SQR-11 |
| Inheritance depth | > 3 project-defined levels | SQR-21 |

#### Elements

| ID | Smell | Criterion (fail when …) | Applies when | Check | ISO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQR-01 | Long Function | A function or method body exceeds 60 logical lines (non-blank, non-comment), or exceeds 30 and does ≥ 2 distinct jobs. Confirm by reading. | any function | SQ-01 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-02 | — | One function mixes abstraction levels: I/O or framework calls, parsing/mapping and business rules interleaved in one body. | any function > 20 lines | SQ-01 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-03 | — | Estimated cyclomatic complexity > 15 (1 + each `if`, `else if`, `case`, loop, `catch`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `?:`, `??`, comprehension `if`). | any function | SQ-02 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-04 | — | Control-flow nesting deeper than 4 levels. | any function | SQ-02 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-05 | — | A condition with > 3 boolean operands, or a negated compound condition, is written inline and unnamed in a branch. | any branch | SQ-02 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-06 | Duplicated Code | ≥ 10 consecutive lines that are identical apart from identifiers or literals appear in ≥ 2 places in the reviewed files. | ≥ 2 reviewed files or functions | SQ-03 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-07 | Repeated Switches | The same `switch`/`if` chain on the same type code or discriminator appears in ≥ 3 places. | type-code branching | SQ-03 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-08 | Large Class | A class or module > 500 lines, or > 20 public methods, or > 10 constructor-injected dependencies. Confirm by reading. | any class/module | SQ-04 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-09 | Divergent Change | One class owns unrelated responsibilities (e.g. `*Manager`/`*Helper`/`*Utils` mixing persistence, formatting and business rules). | any class | SQ-04 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-10 | Feature Envy | A method uses another object's data and methods more than its own, so the behavior belongs elsewhere. | any method | SQ-04 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-11 | Long Parameter List | More than 5 parameters (excluding constructor dependency injection, which SQR-08 covers). | any function | SQ-05 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-12 | Data Clumps | The same group of ≥ 3 parameters or fields recurs together in ≥ 2 signatures or classes. | ≥ 2 signatures | SQ-05 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-13 | Flag Argument | A boolean or enum argument only selects which behavior the function performs. | any function | SQ-05 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-14 | — | A catch-all (`catch (Exception)`, `catch (Throwable)`, `except Exception`) appears below a process or request boundary without translating, rethrowing or a documented reason. (Empty or unlogged catches are SEC-OP-02.) | exception handling present | SQ-06 | ISO-19 |
| SQR-15 | — | Exceptions are used for normal control flow, e.g. thrown and caught in the same method to break a loop, or to test existence. | exception handling present | SQ-06 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-16 | — | Thrown exceptions are generic (`Exception`, `RuntimeException`, bare `raise Exception("…")`) where a specific built-in or domain type exists. | code throws | SQ-06 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-17 | Dead Code | Unreachable code, private members never referenced in the reviewed files, or parameters never read. (Reachable superseded code is MAINT-05.) | any file | SQ-08 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-18 | — | A block of ≥ 3 consecutive commented-out code lines. | any file | SQ-08 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-19 | Global Data | A singleton, static field or module-level global holds per-request or per-user mutable state in a server context (web handlers, workers). | server code | DP-01 | ISO-02 |
| SQR-20 | Mutable Data | Shared static or singleton mutable state is changed from concurrent code without synchronization or a concurrent collection. | concurrent code | DP-01 | ISO-17 |
| SQR-21 | — | An inheritance chain of > 3 project-defined levels (framework base classes not counted). | class hierarchies | DP-02 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-22 | Refused Bequest | A subclass overrides inherited members to throw "not supported" or do nothing, or uses only a small part of its base. | class hierarchies | DP-02 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-23 | Middle Man / Speculative Generality | A pass-through class whose methods mostly delegate unchanged, or an abstraction with one implementation and no use as a test, DI or plugin seam. | abstractions present | DP-04 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-24 | — | A type is named for a pattern it doesn't implement, or implements one without the varying problem (a "Factory" that only calls `new` with no choice, a "Strategy" with one strategy and no seam). | pattern names present | DP-04 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-25 | — | Complex construction (≥ 4 optional settings or a multi-step setup) is repeated at ≥ 2 call sites instead of a factory, builder or options object. | complex construction | DP-05 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-26 | — | A subscription to a longer-lived publisher (`+=` events, `addListener`, observables, signal handlers) is never removed or disposed. | event subscriptions | DP-06 | ISO-17 |
| SQR-27 | — | Presentation or API code (controllers, handlers, views, endpoints) directly uses data-access primitives (`DbContext`/`DbSet`, `EntityManager`, JDBC `Connection`, SQLAlchemy `Session`, raw SQL) instead of the business or data layer, in a codebase that has such a layer. | layered code | AP-01 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-28 | — | Business rules (validation beyond request shape, calculations, state transitions) live in controllers or handlers and aren't reused through the domain layer. | layered code | AP-02 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-29 | — | A dependency cycle among reviewed projects, packages or modules (project references, `import` chains), or a lower layer importing a higher one. | ≥ 2 modules | AP-03 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-30 | Shotgun Surgery | One change would have to touch many unrelated modules, or one module mixes unrelated domain areas. (Repository-level layout is MAINT-02.) | ≥ 2 modules | AP-04 | ISO-27 |
| SQR-31 | — | The same cross-cutting code (auth checks, logging scaffolding, input validation, error mapping) is repeated in ≥ 3 handlers instead of middleware, filters, decorators or aspects. | ≥ 3 handlers | AP-06 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-32 | Mysterious Name | Names don't reveal intent: single letters outside loops and lambdas, misleading or type-encoded names, meaningless abbreviations, inconsistent terms for one concept. | any code | CS-01 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-33 | — | Formatting (indentation, braces, spacing, line breaks) is inconsistent within the reviewed files, and no formatter or `.editorconfig` configuration enforces it. | any code | CS-02 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-34 | Comments | Comments restate the code, are stale or contradict it, or explain *what* where a better name would do. Missing *why* on non-obvious decisions. (TODO/FIXME tracking is MAINT-04.) | comments present | CS-03 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-35 | — | Exported or public functions, classes and modules lack documentation comments (generic rule for languages without a localized guide). | language not C#/Java/Python | CS-04 | ISO-29 |
| SQR-36 | — | Static checking that the project has adopted isn't applied consistently: C# `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` with nullable warnings suppressed or ignored; a Python type checker configured (mypy/pyright) but public signatures unannotated; Java nullness annotations used inconsistently. | the project opts in (config present) | CS-05 | ISO-30 |
| SQR-37 | — | Multi-step business workflows (checkout, approval, onboarding) don't validate state transitions on the server: no state machine or equivalent guard, so steps can be skipped, repeated or reordered by calling endpoints directly, or sequencing is left to the front end. Reference: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet `#preventing-out-of-order-api-execution` (@97cb8a3c). | multi-step workflow exposed through separate endpoints or handlers | AP-02 | ISO-22 |

## File: `references/standards/iso-25010.md`

*Load rule: ISO-01…ISO-40 (classification only). Always load.*

### ISO/IEC 25010:2023 product quality model — localized summary

- **Classification only.** ISO elements belong to no check, never fail on their own and never appear in
  `Finding.standard`. Each Software Quality, Design Patterns and Architecture Patterns finding names one in its
  `title` suffix, e.g. `[ISO 25010:2023 Maintainability › Analysability, ISO-29]`.

| ID | Characteristic › Sub-characteristic | Definition (summary) |
|---|---|---|
| ISO-01 | Functional suitability › Functional completeness | Functions cover all specified tasks and user objectives. |
| ISO-02 | Functional suitability › Functional correctness | Functions give accurate results. |
| ISO-03 | Functional suitability › Functional appropriateness | Functions help users accomplish their tasks. |
| ISO-04 | Performance efficiency › Time behaviour | Response time and throughput meet requirements. |
| ISO-05 | Performance efficiency › Resource utilization | Amounts and types of resources used meet requirements. |
| ISO-06 | Performance efficiency › Capacity | Maximum limits of parameters meet requirements. |
| ISO-07 | Compatibility › Co-existence | Runs alongside other products in a shared environment without harm. |
| ISO-08 | Compatibility › Interoperability | Exchanges information with other systems and uses it. |
| ISO-09 | Interaction capability › Appropriateness recognizability | Users can recognize whether the product suits their needs. |
| ISO-10 | Interaction capability › Learnability | Functions can be learned within a set time. |
| ISO-11 | Interaction capability › Operability | Easy to operate and control. |
| ISO-12 | Interaction capability › User error protection | Prevents operation errors. |
| ISO-13 | Interaction capability › User engagement | The interface is inviting and encourages continued use. |
| ISO-14 | Interaction capability › Inclusivity | Usable by people of varied backgrounds and abilities. |
| ISO-15 | Interaction capability › User assistance | Users with a wide range of characteristics achieve their goals. |
| ISO-16 | Interaction capability › Self-descriptiveness | Capabilities and use are obvious without extra resources. |
| ISO-17 | Reliability › Faultlessness | Performs specified functions without faults in normal operation. |
| ISO-18 | Reliability › Availability | Operational and accessible when needed. |
| ISO-19 | Reliability › Fault tolerance | Keeps operating as intended despite faults. |
| ISO-20 | Reliability › Recoverability | Recovers data and restores state after a failure. |
| ISO-21 | Security › Confidentiality | Data accessible only to authorized parties. |
| ISO-22 | Security › Integrity | Protected from unauthorized modification or deletion. |
| ISO-23 | Security › Non-repudiation | Actions can be proven so they can't be denied later. |
| ISO-24 | Security › Accountability | Actions trace uniquely to an entity. |
| ISO-25 | Security › Authenticity | Claimed identity can be proven. |
| ISO-26 | Security › Resistance | Sustains operations under attack. |
| ISO-27 | Maintainability › Modularity | Discrete components; a change to one has minimal impact on others. |
| ISO-28 | Maintainability › Reusability | Usable as an asset in more than one system. |
| ISO-29 | Maintainability › Analysability | Impact of changes, deficiencies and parts to modify can be assessed. |
| ISO-30 | Maintainability › Modifiability | Can be changed without introducing defects or degrading quality. |
| ISO-31 | Maintainability › Testability | Test criteria can be set and tests run against them. |
| ISO-32 | Flexibility › Adaptability | Can be adapted to different hardware, software or environments. |
| ISO-33 | Flexibility › Scalability | Handles growing or shrinking workloads by adjusting capacity. |
| ISO-34 | Flexibility › Installability | Can be installed and uninstalled effectively. |
| ISO-35 | Flexibility › Replaceability | Can replace another product with the same purpose. |
| ISO-36 | Safety › Operational constraint | Keeps operation within safe parameters when hazards occur. |
| ISO-37 | Safety › Risk identification | Identifies event sequences that expose people or property to unacceptable risk. |
| ISO-38 | Safety › Fail safe | Automatically enters a safe mode on failure. |
| ISO-39 | Safety › Hazard warning | Warns of unacceptable risks in time to act. |
| ISO-40 | Safety › Safe integration | Maintains safety during and after integration. |

Most findings of this skill map to ISO-27 … ISO-31 (Maintainability), ISO-17/ISO-19 (exception design, shared
state) and ISO-02 (correctness defects). The rubric's ISO column gives the default per element.

## File: `references/standards/azure-architecture.md`

*Load rule: AAS-01…AAS-20. Always load.*

### Azure Architecture Center: architecture styles and "Design for change" — localized summary

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.
- The N-tier layer rules sit in the page introduction, which has no anchor: those rows cite `nt` without a fragment.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| AAS-01 | Each layer has one responsibility. A higher layer may use a lower layer, but a lower layer never uses a higher one. | layered code | AP-03 |
| AAS-02 | In a closed-layer design a layer calls only the next layer down. Skipping layers (open layers) is a deliberate, documented choice because it adds coupling. | layered code | AP-01 |
| AAS-03 | The data tier is accessed only from the middle (business) tier. | layered code | AP-01 |
| AAS-04 | A middle tier that only passes CRUD calls through adds latency and complexity without value. | layered code | DP-04 |
| AAS-05 | A chosen architecture style constrains which elements exist and how they may relate. Code that only superficially conforms loses the style's benefits. | ≥ 2 deployable units | AP-07 |
| AAS-06 | Architectural complexity matches the domain. Too little structure produces a "big ball of mud" with unmanaged dependencies. | ≥ 2 modules | AP-04 |
| AAS-07 | Each service implements a single business capability within a bounded context, and services aren't overly granular. | microservices | AP-07 |
| AAS-08 | Data is private to the owning service: no shared database schemas or direct access to another service's store. | microservices | AP-07 |
| AAS-09 | Services don't share common domain libraries or code that couples their release cycles. | microservices | AP-07 |
| AAS-10 | Gateways handle routing and infrastructure only. They contain no domain knowledge or business rules. | gateway/BFF code in scope | AP-02 |
| AAS-11 | Database entities aren't used as events or API payloads. Contracts model the domain, not the internal implementation. | ≥ 2 deployable units | AP-07 |
| AAS-12 | Security logic such as token validation isn't embedded in each service's business code. It's offloaded to a dedicated component, gateway or middleware. | ≥ 2 handlers or services | AP-06 |
| AAS-13 | Cross-cutting concerns are offloaded to a separate component (gateway, sidecar, shared middleware) so they evolve without touching every consumer. | ≥ 2 handlers or services | AP-06 |
| AAS-14 | Common infrastructure tasks are abstracted (framework or library) instead of repeated as error-prone code in each service. | ≥ 2 handlers or services | AP-06 |
| AAS-15 | Web front end and worker communicate through the queue. Shared data schemas or code modules between them create hidden dependencies. | web + worker in scope | AP-07 |
| AAS-16 | The front end and worker don't grow into large monolithic components. | web + worker in scope | AP-04 |
| AAS-17 | High cohesion and loose coupling: functionality that changes together lives together, and needing coordinated updates across modules shows low cohesion. | ≥ 2 modules | AP-04 |
| AAS-18 | Domain knowledge is encapsulated in the module or service that owns it. Clients don't each enforce the business rules. | layered code | AP-02 |
| AAS-19 | Infrastructure (messaging, persistence) is abstracted away from domain logic. | layered code | AP-02 |
| AAS-20 | Overly chatty communication between two modules or services signals tight coupling and low cohesion. (The latency impact is performance's concern.) | ≥ 2 modules | AP-04 |

## File: `references/standards/fowler-bliki.md`

*Load rule: MFB-01…MFB-06. Always load.*

### Martin Fowler bliki — localized summary

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| MFB-01 | Presentation, domain logic and data access are separated, and dependencies run presentation → domain → data, never upwards. | layered code | AP-01 |
| MFB-02 | Validations and calculations belong in the domain layer, not in UI or controller code (which is also harder to test). | layered code | AP-02 |
| MFB-03 | The domain treats data sources as abstractions. The data layer converts storage formats, optionally through a mapper so the domain doesn't depend on storage. | layered code | AP-02 |
| MFB-04 | When a layer grows too large, the top level is split into domain-oriented modules, each layered internally. | ≥ 2 modules | AP-04 |
| MFB-05 | A code smell is a quickly spotted indication of a deeper problem that needs investigation. It isn't always a problem (the basis of the threshold-plus-confirmation rule). | any SQ-01 finding | SQ-01 |
| MFB-06 | A data class with no behavior, whose logic lives in other classes, is a smell. Ask what behavior should move into it. (DTOs and records at boundaries are exempt.) | domain-layer classes | SQ-04 |

## File: `references/standards/fowler-refactoring-catalog.md`

*Load rule: FRC-01…FRC-23 (remedies only). Always load.*

### Refactoring catalog (2nd edition) — localized summary, remedies only

- **Remedies only.** FRC elements never fail on their own and never appear in `Finding.standard`. Name them in
  `recommendation`, e.g. "Apply *Extract Function* (FRC-01, https://refactoring.com/catalog/extractFunction.html)".

| ID | Refactoring (remedy) | Use for | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| FRC-01 | Extract Function (1st ed.: Extract Method) | Long Function (SQR-01) | SQ-01 |
| FRC-02 | Split Phase | Mixed abstraction levels (SQR-02) | SQ-01 |
| FRC-03 | Decompose Conditional | Complex branches (SQR-03, SQR-05) | SQ-02 |
| FRC-04 | Consolidate Conditional Expression | Long boolean chains (SQR-05) | SQ-02 |
| FRC-05 | Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses | Deep nesting (SQR-04) | SQ-02 |
| FRC-06 | Replace Conditional with Polymorphism | Repeated Switches (SQR-07) | SQ-03 |
| FRC-07 | Replace Inline Code with Function Call | Duplicated Code (SQR-06) | SQ-03 |
| FRC-08 | Parameterize Function | Near-duplicate functions (SQR-06) | SQ-03 |
| FRC-09 | Extract Class | Large Class, divergent responsibilities (SQR-08, SQR-09) | SQ-04 |
| FRC-10 | Move Function | Feature Envy, data classes (SQR-10, MFB-06) | SQ-04 |
| FRC-11 | Introduce Parameter Object | Long Parameter List, Data Clumps (SQR-11, SQR-12) | SQ-05 |
| FRC-12 | Preserve Whole Object | Long Parameter List (SQR-11) | SQ-05 |
| FRC-13 | Remove Flag Argument | Flag arguments (SQR-13) | SQ-05 |
| FRC-14 | Replace Exception with Precheck | Exceptions as control flow (SQR-15) | SQ-06 |
| FRC-15 | Remove Dead Code | Dead or commented-out code (SQR-17, SQR-18) | SQ-08 |
| FRC-16 | Encapsulate Variable | Global or mutable shared data (SQR-19, SQR-20) | DP-01 |
| FRC-17 | Replace Superclass with Delegate | Refused Bequest, deep inheritance (SQR-21, SQR-22) | DP-02 |
| FRC-18 | Collapse Hierarchy | Needless hierarchy levels (SQR-21) | DP-02 |
| FRC-19 | Remove Middle Man | Pass-through classes (SQR-23, AAS-04) | DP-04 |
| FRC-20 | Inline Class | Speculative abstractions (SQR-23, SQR-24) | DP-04 |
| FRC-21 | Replace Constructor with Factory Function | Duplicated complex construction (SQR-25) | DP-05 |
| FRC-22 | Rename Variable / Rename Field / Change Function Declaration | Mysterious Name (SQR-32, MSC-06) | CS-01 |
| FRC-23 | Replace Magic Literal | Unnamed literals that obscure intent (SQR-32) | CS-01 |
